analysis.title: GS Healthcare Trading Preview 11.19.26
key_insights: Policy headlines drove a sharp selloff in Managed Care on Nov 18: HUM -13% and UNH -10%. The weakness spilled over to broader Hospitals/Services and marginally to Large Pharma.

The drivers were CMS's unexpected proposed rule, CRUSH, which puts risk adjustment data validation (RADV) audits and the wider Medicare Advantage policy outlook back in focus, and renewed Medicare for All (M4A) headlines from Democratic senators.
The desk notes significant investor debate and pushback on the likelihood of sweeping policy change, despite the size of the move.

Investors had increasingly viewed the recent Medicare Advantage reimbursement reset as receding. CRUSH reverses that view. GS expects political headlines on M4A and vertical integration to recur over the coming years.
GIR published a note on the MCO group since CRUSH and the 'Blue Sweep'. The desk expects broader macro and market focus to dominate attention on Nov 19.
MRK announced a research collaboration with Isomorphic Labs on small molecule candidates against a strategically important oncology target. Merck pays an upfront amount plus milestones and royalties.

NVS reiterated its 2025-30 group net sales target of +5-6% cc CAGR and its 2029 core operating income margin guide of 40%+. It rolled the mid-term guide forward to 2026-31 with a +5% cc sales CAGR against consensus of 4.3%.
GIR says the NVS guide is broadly in line with its estimates and implies c.3% upside risk to company consensus sales and operating profit in 2031.

NVS management expects a mid-single-digit % CAGR long term after 2030, while consensus is at -1%. That leaves a c.$20bn sales gap between guidance and consensus due to patent expirations. GIR expects the plan to fill this gap to be the focus of the Nov 19 Meet the Management event.

The FDA approved Regeneron's Livsayis (cemdisiran) for generalized myasthenia gravis. It is Regeneron's first approved siRNA therapy and first neurology medicine. Approval rests on Phase 3 NIMBLE data showing disease control maintained through three-month dosing intervals.
Leerink Partners upgraded ABT to Outperform.
Most active names the prior trading day: VTRS, BNTX, PFE, SRPT, WAT, CTY.

Sonic Healthcare (SHL.AX) is listed with EBITDA guidance reiterated. No figures are given.

Medicare for All and vertical-integration headlines from Democratic senators are expected to recur over the coming years.
NVS faces a c.$20bn sales gap after 2030 from patent expirations. Consensus is at -1% CAGR against management's mid-single-digit expectation.
